requirements.text: open a new case under the Employee Profile Update service, assign it to Travis Wood, and route it to the HR Service Desk group

cells.short_description: LIKE '%Service: Employee Profile Update, Subject: Daniel Clark, Detail:%'

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 35 AND opened_for = 66 AND assigned_to = 11 AND assignment_group = 4 AND status = 'work_in_progress' AND priority = 'moderate' AND source = 'phone' AND account_number = 'NA' AND coe_type = 'Workforce Administration' AND short_description LIKE '%Service: Employee Profile Update, Subject: Daniel Clark, Detail:%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id in the seed is 60); the task creates exactly one case
Employee Profile Update is hr_service 35 (active); Daniel Clark is user 66 with hr_profile 66, the only Daniel Clark; Travis Wood is user 11; HR Service Desk is group 4
status work_in_progress: the policy sets it upon assigning a case to a user, and ready to work_in_progress is a valid transition
priority moderate: 'sooner rather than later' names no priority level, so the policy's default applies
account number not provided; the policy requires NA
coe_type Workforce Administration kept from the benchmark check; it matches the service's topic (topic_detail 28, whose category carries coe_type Workforce Administration)
short description follows the policy's 'Service: , Subject: , Detail: ' format; the Detail text is free, so only the prefix is tested, with Daniel Clark as the subject kept from the benchmark check

requirements.text: assign it to Travis Wood, and route it to the HR Service Desk group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 44 AND group_id = 4 AND user_id = 11
assumptions: Travis Wood (user 11) is a member of group 3 (Global Service Desk) only, not of HR Service Desk (group 4); the policy requires adding the assignee to the assignment group when not a member
implied by the request, not stated
id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id in the seed is 43); the task creates exactly one membership

requirements.text: send Daniel an update confirming that the request has been logged and share the current case status on his work email
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND email = 'daniel.clark81@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update' AND status = 'work_in_progress'
assumptions: two notifications are created with no fixed order, so this one is selected by case and recipient rather than by id
his work email is the user email daniel.clark81@servicenow.com, not the personal email on his hr_profile
status work_in_progress is the case's current status after assignment, which the request asks the notification to share

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND email = 'travis.wood@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update' AND status = 'work_in_progress'
assumptions: the policy requires an update notification with the current case status to the assigned agent when a case moves into work_in_progress
implied by the request, not stated
selected by case and recipient rather than by id, since two notifications are created
Travis Wood's address is his user email, travis.wood@servicenow.com

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on every requirement, value and disposition; no disagreements.
The acting user is Robin Monroe (user 31, manager), who may create and assign cases.
The benchmark's case check has no id; the case is anchored at 61, which the benchmark's notification checks already assume.
opened_by is not tested: the policy makes it the requester, and here either Daniel Clark (who called and asked HR to look) or Robin Monroe (who asks for the case to be opened) could be that requester.
The Detail part of the short description and request_status are not fixed by the request or policy and are not tested.
Service 35 has no service template, so moving the case to work_in_progress generates no fulfilment tasks.
